title: extends / super
description: extends sets the prototype chain; super() calls the parent constructor; super.method() calls a parent method from an override.

notes: In a subclass constructor you MUST call super(...) before touching this — otherwise ReferenceError.
super.method() inside a method calls the parent version; super alone in a constructor calls the parent constructor.
instanceof walks the prototype chain — a Dog is also an Animal.

questions.q: Which keyword sets up class inheritance?
What happens if you use `this` before calling super() in a subclass constructor?
Inside an overridden method, how do you call the parent version?
For `class Dog extends Animal {}` and `const d = new Dog()`, what is `d instanceof Animal`?

exercises.prompt: Override speak() and call the parent version with super.
Add a subclass field and verify instanceof walks up the chain.

L3.prompt: Build `Animal` with describe() returning the name, and `Dog extends Animal` whose describe() returns parent describe + " the " + breed. Log `new Dog("Rex", "lab").describe()`.
hints: Call super(name) first in the Dog constructor.
In Dog.describe(), compose super.describe() with " the " + this.breed.
